questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: Why do we need political parties?
questions.stem: A student complains that people in the country hold far too many different opinions on what policies are suitable for society, and that no government can handle all of them. Explain in about 45 words how a political party deals with this, and what a government is then expected to do.

markingPoints.description: States that a large number of similar opinions have to be grouped together to provide a direction in which policies can be formulated by the governments
States that a party reduces a vast multitude of opinions into a few basic positions which it supports
States that a government is expected to base its policies on the line taken by the ruling party

answerScheme.modelAnswer: A large number of similar opinions have to be grouped together to provide a direction in which policies can be formulated. A party reduces a vast multitude of opinions into a few basic positions which it supports. A government is expected to base its policies on the line taken by the ruling party.

questions.topic: Why do we need political parties?
questions.stem: Most of the members of a legislature belong to one political party, and a law is being debated and passed. Explain in about 45 words why the members vote the way their party leadership tells them, even where that goes against their personal opinions.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: Why do we need political parties?
questions.stem: A student is asked to explain to the class why modern democracies cannot exist without political parties. Set out, in steps, what political parties actually do to fill political offices and exercise political power.

markingPoints.description: Political parties fill political offices and exercise political power by performing a series of functions
They contest elections, and in most democracies elections are fought mainly among the candidates put up by political parties
They put forward different policies and programmes and the voters choose from them
They play a decisive role in making laws for a country
They form and run governments by recruiting leaders, training them and then making them ministers to run the government in the way they want

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Step 1: Parties contest elections - in most democracies, elections are fought mainly among the candidates put up by political parties.
Step 2: Parties put forward different policies and programmes and the voters choose from them.
Step 3: Parties play a decisive role in making laws for a country.
Step 4: Parties form and run governments - they recruit leaders, train them and then make them ministers to run the government in the way they want.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.topic: Why do we need political parties?
questions.stem: Two students compare elections in India and in the USA. Set out, in steps, the different ways in which political parties select their candidates for contesting elections, and say which of these methods more and more countries are now following.

markingPoints.description: Parties select their candidates in different ways
In some countries, such as the USA, members and supporters of a party choose its candidates
Now more and more countries are following this method
In other countries like India, top party leaders choose candidates for contesting elections
In most democracies, elections are fought mainly among the candidates put up by political parties

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Step 1: Parties select their candidates in different ways.
Step 2: In some countries, such as the USA, members and supporters of a party choose its candidates.
Step 3: Now more and more countries are following this method.
Step 4: In other countries like India, top party leaders choose candidates for contesting elections.
Step 5: In most democracies, elections are fought mainly among the candidates put up by political parties.

questions.stem: A student in Delhi asks why national parties can no longer be sure of winning a Lok Sabha majority on their own, and what they now have to do about it. Set out, in steps, what has changed and what has followed from it.

No one national party is able to secure on its own a majority in the Lok Sabha, until 2014
As a result, the national parties are compelled to form alliances with State parties
Since 1996, nearly every one of the State parties has got an opportunity to be a part of one national level political organisation or the other national level coalition
This has contributed to the strengthening of federalism and democracy in the country

Step 3: As a result, the national parties are compelled to form alliances with State parties.
Step 4: Since 1996, nearly every State party has joined a national level organisation or coalition, strengthening federalism and democracy.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.stem:
On an outline map of India, locate and label the following:
(a) The State in which the Bahujan Samaj Party has its main base.
(b) A neighbouring State in which the Bahujan Samaj Party has a substantial presence.
(c) The State which the Bharatiya Janata Party wants to see fully integrated with India.
(d) A State in which the Communist Party of India - Marxist enjoys strong support.
(e) Another State in which the Communist Party of India - Marxist enjoys strong support.

markingPoints.description: Uttar Pradesh - the State in which the Bahujan Samaj Party has its main base
Madhya Pradesh - a neighbouring State in which the Bahujan Samaj Party has a substantial presence
Jammu and Kashmir - the State which the Bharatiya Janata Party wants to see fully integrated with India
West Bengal - a State in which the Communist Party of India - Marxist enjoys strong support
Kerala - another State in which the Communist Party of India - Marxist enjoys strong support

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
(a) Uttar Pradesh, the main base of the Bahujan Samaj Party.
(b) Madhya Pradesh, one of the neighbouring States where it has a substantial presence; Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh, Delhi and Punjab are others.
(c) Jammu and Kashmir, whose full territorial and political integration with India the Bharatiya Janata Party wants.
(d) West Bengal, where the Communist Party of India - Marxist enjoys strong support.
(e) Kerala, another State where the Communist Party of India - Marxist enjoys strong support; Tripura is also named.
